correctness.rationale: PASS is for the corrected files under repairs/2, not the frozen wording. The frozen Finding and slogan overstate the distinction of the rank-one convergence rate: for α=4−2√2 the generic root norm factor √|1−α| and rank-one factor 1−α/2 are both √2−1. Also, an eventual contrast √c is fixed rather than of least period two. The repair states both exceptions and leaves the exact matrix and rank-loss classifications intact. Re-audit: for d=1−α and mean a, the first signed entries a(d±r) give contrast r/c below c, rank loss at c, and c/r above c. For r_0=c^x the first branch subtracts one from x, giving exactly update k for integer x=k, and entry at floor(x) otherwise. The upper branch is an involution with sole fixed point √c; the repaired example α=3/4, E_0=diag(3,1) verifies the distinction. In that branch the second step uses mean ar and polar signs (+,−), giving ad(1±r) and hence E_{t+2}=dE_t in the original frames. Both parity subsequences then have per-update root factor √c. At rank one the active thin polar gives the positive multiplier 1−α/2, and equal singular values give d per step. Solving equality of the two asserted factors gives the unique rate-coincidence step in the interval. The replacement RESULT.md, SLOGAN.txt and REVIEW.md no longer claim universal rate separation or universal least period two. The frozen rational/numerical checker was inspected, not run; it tests the unchanged identities and is not a proof of any infinite-time result.

value.rationale: The repaired statement gives the complete rank and orbit behavior for the first nontrivial row dimension under fixed steps, not another general convergence bound. Exact rank loss at prescribed powers and a finite entry time into a signed two-step scaling law are useful benchmarks for the polar update. The equality of the two root norm factors at one allowed step shows why rank behavior cannot be read solely from convergence exponents; the value does not depend on the false universal rate separation.
